repo_notes.content: ipparse is written in MoonScript: the `.moon` files are the source of truth; the `.lua` files beside them are generated by `moonc` and ignored by git (only a few hand-written Lua files are tracked: `lib/sha.lua`, `lib/sha2.lua`, `lib/util.lua`). Show code samples in MoonScript, not Lua. The library targets two runtimes — Lunatik (Lua in the Linux kernel) and plain Lua/LuaJIT in userspace — so modules must stay small and allocation-light: in the kernel hot path, avoid superfluous allocations (no throwaway tables or per-packet string concatenation). Kernel loading also spends C stack, so `require "ipparse"` must be the first `require` of every entry module (see `ipparse/AGENTS.md`). `ipparse/doc/` is LDoc output generated from the sources with `ldoc .`, not hand-written documentation; cite the modules instead. The module contract (`parse` / `pack` / `new`, no `class`, metatables) is described in `ipparse/.agents/architecture.md`.

pages.title: MoonTAStik Overview
pages.purpose: Introduce MoonTAStik as a MoonScript collection for Lunatik, describing the ipparse library and the hexdump tool, both released under MIT OR GPL-2.0-only.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain how a packet flows through the library from a pcap source down to Layer 7 and how the hexdump tool hooks into the kernel, with the runtime constraints this imposes.

pages.title: ipparse Library
pages.purpose: Overview of the ipparse library: package layout, the parse/pack/new contract, metatable-based OOP without classes, and the layered parsing model.

pages.title: Core Utilities and Lua Compatibility
pages.purpose: Document the shared helpers in init.moon, the functional primitives in fun/ (iter, memo, bidirectional, opairs, protected), and the bit/pack shims that let the same code run on LuaJIT, Lua 5.1 to 5.5 and the kernel.

page_notes.content: Explain that bit_compat selects its native backend by capability before any pcall, so a kernel C stack overflow propagates instead of being masked by a generic fallback error; mention bit_pure and pack_compat as the last-resort paths.

pages.title: Layer 2: Ethernet Protocol
pages.purpose: Document Ethernet frame parsing and packing in l2/ethernet.moon, including MAC address handling and EtherType dispatch to the next layer.

pages.title: Layer 3: IP Processing
pages.purpose: Explain the unified IP entry point in l3/ip.moon that detects the IP version and dispatches to the IPv4 or IPv6 modules.

pages.title: IPv4 Protocol
pages.purpose: Detail l3/ip4.moon: header parsing and packing, options, address conversion and checksum handling.

pages.title: IPv6 Protocol
pages.purpose: Detail l3/ip6.moon: header parsing and packing, extension headers, address conversion and key derivation helpers.

pages.title: IPv4 Fragmentation Handling
pages.purpose: Explain l3/fragmented_ip4.moon: tracking fragments per datagram and reassembling IPv4 packets, including its bounds and eviction policy.

pages.title: Layer 4: Transport Protocols
pages.purpose: Overview of transport layer support in l4/, covering TCP, UDP, their port/service mappings and QUIC, and how each module advertises its payload offset.

pages.title: TCP Protocol
pages.purpose: Document l4/tcp.moon: header parsing and packing, flag management through the metatable, and checksum support.

pages.title: UDP Protocol
pages.purpose: Document l4/udp.moon: header parsing and packing, length validation and payload extraction.

pages.title: TCP Stream Reassembly
pages.purpose: Explain l4/tcp_stream.moon: the stateful defragmenter that accumulates payloads per session key, clears on FIN/RST, purges by age and bounds memory per session and in total.

pages.title: Port Number Mappings
pages.purpose: Explain l4/tcp_ports.moon and l4/udp_ports.moon, the bidirectional tables mapping service names to port numbers and back.

pages.title: QUIC Protocol
pages.purpose: Document QUIC header handling in l4/quic/: long and short header dispatch, connection IDs, versions and version negotiation packets.

pages.title: QUIC Initial Packet Decryption
pages.purpose: Explain l4/quic/v1/keys.moon and v1/protection.moon: RFC 9001 key derivation from the connection ID, header protection removal, packet number nonce construction and AEAD decryption of Initial packets.

page_notes.content: protection.moon is backend-agnostic: every cryptographic operation is delegated to a backend table passed as argument. Do not present OpenSSL, mbedTLS or wolfSSL as a hard requirement.

pages.title: QUIC Frames
pages.purpose: Document l4/quic/frames.moon: VarInt decoding, CRYPTO, STREAM, ACK and control frame parsing and packing, and the frame iterator.

pages.title: QUIC SNI Extraction
pages.purpose: Explain l7/quic/session.moon: the stateful helper that consumes raw QUIC datagrams, decrypts Initial packets, reassembles the CRYPTO stream and extracts the TLS SNI.

pages.title: Layer 7: Application Protocols
pages.purpose: Overview of application layer support in l7/: DNS, TLS and the QUIC-to-TLS bridge used for SNI extraction.

pages.title: DNS Protocol
pages.purpose: Document l7/dns.moon: message parsing and packing, name label compression, question and resource record handling and EDNS support.

pages.title: TLS Protocol
pages.purpose: Document the TLS record layer and the module layout of l7/tls/, and how records are dispatched to the handshake parser.

pages.title: TLS Handshake Processing
pages.purpose: Explain l7/tls/handshake/init.moon: handshake message dispatch, cipher suites, compression methods, extensions and key derivation.

pages.title: TLS ClientHello Messages
pages.purpose: Detail l7/tls/handshake/client_hello.moon: ClientHello structure, parsing and packing of its fields.

pages.title: TLS Extensions
pages.purpose: Document l7/tls/handshake/extension/: the extension registry, Server Name Indication and supported versions, their parsing and packing.

pages.title: Crypto Backends and Primitives
pages.purpose: Describe the backend contract in lib/crypto/init.moon, the lunatik, ffi_openssl, ffi_mbedtls and ffi_wolfssl backends, and the HKDF and SHA helpers they build on.

page_notes.content: The FFI backends are optional: when OpenSSL or mbedTLS cannot be loaded, their tests skip themselves rather than fail. Describe them as optional accelerators, not as required dependencies.

pages.title: PCAP and PCAPNG Reading
pages.purpose: Document lib/pcap.moon: reading PCAP and PCAPNG files, section and interface description blocks, and yielding packet payloads with timestamps.

pages.title: hexdump Tool
pages.purpose: Document the kernel packet inspection tool in hexdump/: its XDP C hook, the MoonScript side that formats packets, and how to build and load it under Lunatik.

pages.title: Build, Packaging and Release
pages.purpose: Explain the Makefiles, MoonScript compilation with moonc, installation into the kernel module tree with source or bytecode, the LuaRocks rockspec and the moontastik_lua.zip release consumed by Lunatik.

pages.title: Testing and CI
pages.purpose: Describe the test suite in ipparse/tests/ (run_all, malformed input, kernel stack canary, luacov coverage against a baseline), the virtme-ng microVM kernel tests in tools/vmtest/, and the GitHub Actions pipeline that runs them.

page_notes.content: State that REQUIRE_DEPTH in tests/test_lunatik_kernel_stack_canary.moon must never be lowered to make the suite pass: it is the mechanical guard for the kernel stack budget.

pages.title: Examples and Usage
pages.purpose: Walk through the MoonScript examples in ipparse/examples/: parsing a pcap capture, decoding DNS and TLS, and extracting the SNI from real QUIC traffic.
